data.narrative:
Astrolight, a seed-stage Space & Aerospace company founded by Laurynas Mačiulis, has raised €2.8M to date. The sector encompasses 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and a broader private peer set including Starcloud, SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, and Sierra Space, though narrow-stage peer data remains sparse.

Of three valuation methods assessed, only stage-progression proved applicable. Using total capital raised (€2.8M / ~$3M) as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a typical 2.5x multiplier for progression from seed to the next institutional stage yields an implied valuation of $7M. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied absent disclosed revenue figures—standard for private companies—though the Space & Aerospace sector trades at a 25.3x P/S median across public peers. Peer-median triangulation was inapplicable due to insufficient same- and adjacent-stage private comparables within the sector (fewer than three datapoints meeting narrow filters).

The analysis supports a valuation range of $6M to $8M, with a $7M midpoint. This range reflects limited triangulation depth; key uncertainties include the absence of revenue or unit economics data, scarcity of seed-stage private peer valuations in Space & Aerospace, and volatility in public sector multiples. A more robust conclusion would require either additional private comparable transactions or disclosure of Astrolight's near-term revenue trajectory.
